topic: DAA - Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (Single and Infinite Transactions)

questions.questionText: What is the core idea of the greedy algorithm for maximizing stock profit when only one transaction is allowed?
options: Perform all possible transactions regardless of price
Buy and sell on the same day to avoid loss
Buy at the highest price and sell at the lowest price
Buy at the lowest price seen so far and sell at the highest price after that
questions.correctAnswer: Buy at the lowest price seen so far and sell at the highest price after that
questions.explanation: The greedy approach scans the price list, keeps track of the minimum price encountered, and computes profit by selling at the current price; the maximum profit is achieved by buying at the lowest price before a later higher price and selling at that higher price.

questions.questionText: Given the price list [3,9,1,7,2,20] and using the single‑transaction greedy algorithm, what are the current minimum price and maximum profit after processing day 4 (price 7)?
questions.explanation: After day 1 (3) min=3, profit=0. Day 2 (9) gives profit 9‑3=6, so max profit=6. Day 3 (1) updates min to 1, profit stays 6. Day 4 (7) yields 7‑1=6, which does not exceed current max profit, so min remains 1 and max profit stays 6. Hence after day 4 the minimum price is 1 and the maximum profit is 6.

questions.questionText: Given the stock prices over six days: 3, 9, 1, 7, 2, 20, what are the total profits obtained by the single‑transaction greedy approach and the multiple‑transaction greedy approach, and which method yields the higher total profit?
options: Single-transaction profit = 19, multiple-transaction profit = 30, multiple-transaction yields higher total.
Single-transaction profit = 19, multiple-transaction profit = 19, both methods yield the same profit.
Single-transaction profit = 24, multiple-transaction profit = 30, multiple-transaction yields higher total.
Single-transaction profit = 19, multiple-transaction profit = 24, single-transaction yields higher total.
questions.correctAnswer: Single-transaction profit = 19, multiple-transaction profit = 30, multiple-transaction yields higher total.
questions.explanation: The single‑transaction greedy algorithm finds the maximum difference between a low price and a later high price: buy at 1 (day 3) and sell at 20 (day 6) for a profit of 19. The multiple‑transaction greedy algorithm sums all positive day‑to‑day price increases: (9‑3)=6, (7‑1)=6, (20‑2)=18, giving a total profit of 30. Hence the multiple‑transaction approach yields a higher total profit.
